THESE APPEALS, COMING ON FOR HEARING, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 -3-  NC: 2023:KHC:37641  MFA1003/2017 C/W  MFA 1002/2017  JUDGMENT

In these appeals, the petitioners have challenged the common judgment dated 28.09.2016 passed by the III Additional Senior Civil Judge and J.M.F.C., Mangaluru, D.K ('the Tribunal' for short) in M.V.C.No.1565 and 1566 of 2013 in dismissing the claim petitions under Section 163-A of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.

entities.text: III Additional Senior Civil Judge and J.M.F.C., Mangaluru
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. For the sake of convenience, the parties shall be referred to as per their status before the Tribunal.
3. Brief facts of the case are, on 08.02.2013 at about 02:00 pm, one Anand. R. Devadiga was riding the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-19/U-3128 along with pillion rider one Santhosh.

R near Padil of Alape village, the rider lost control of the motor cycle, skidded on the road, dashed on the divider of the road and both were thrown to the right side of the NC: 2023:KHC:37641 MFA1003/2017 C/W road.
At the same time, a tempo bearing Reg.No.KA-19/D-1861 came from opposite direction and dashed against both of them, killing Santhosh.

R at the spot and further injured the rider,
succumbed to death in the hospital.
The petitioners being the dependants have moved the Tribunal for grant of compensation.
Claim was opposed by the Insurance Company.
The Tribunal after taking the evidence, by impugned judgment, dismissed both the claim petitions as not maintainable.
Aggrieved by the same, the petitioners have filed these appeals on various grounds.

4. Heard the arguments of Sri. Ravishankar Shastry. G, learned counsel for the petitioners and Sri.
A.N. Krishnaswamy, learned counsel for the Insurance Company.

5. It is the contention of learned counsel for the petitioners that both the rider and pillion rider were on their way, they have skidded on the road, hit on NC: 2023:KHC:37641 MFA1003/2017 C/W the road divider, due to the impact, they were thrown to the right side of the road.
407 tempo coming from the other side of the road hit, killing both of them.
When the claim is made under Section 163-A of Motor Vehicles Act, there is no question of proving the negligence on part of the tempo.

Hence, the finding recorded by the Tribunal is erroneous and learned counsel further submitted that if an opportunity is provided, the petitioners will lead further evidence to satisfy the Tribunal and sought for remand.
6. Per contra, learned counsel for the Insurance Company has contended that the accident was involving the motor cycle and the 407 tempo.
Claim is made against the 407 tempo without impleading the owner and insurer of the motor cycle.

There is no fault on part of the 407 tempo as it was coming on its correct direction on the other side of the road, both the deceased were at fault, fell Ravindra @ Ravindra Salvankar vs Akshaya Pathra Foundation on 13 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105442862/
3 down on the NC: 2023:KHC:37641 MFA1003/2017 C/W road.

sentences.text: Due to the impact, they were thrown to the other side of the road, therefore 407 tempo has no liability to pay any compensation.
If at all if they have to claim the compensation, it should be against the owner and insurer of the motor cycle.

Learned counsel has no objection for remanding the matter to implead the owner and insurer of the motor cycle and for disposal of the claim in accordance with law.
7.
I have given my anxious consideration to the arguments addressed on both sides and also perused the materials on record.

8. The material on record did point out that both the deceased being rider and pillion rider skidded on the road, hit the road divider, due to the impact, they were thrown to the right side of the road,
both were caught beneath the tempo, they further suffered severe injuries and the pillion rider was killed at the spot, the rider succumbed to death at the hospital.

As further noticed, the pillion rider NC: 2023:KHC:37641 MFA1003/2017 C/W could have filed claim under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, the owner and the insurer of motor cycle should have been impleaded as necessary parties.
Weak drafting of the petition is another example of mofussil pleadings.
Now, the petitioners want to lead additional evidence, they want to implead the owner and the insurer of the motor cycle.

Since the petitioners have lost their bread- earners, it is a fit case where an opportunity may be provided to the petitioners to correct their pleadings, lead further evidence, giving an option to the Tribunal to decide the case on merits in accordance with law is necessary in the ends of justice.

Hence, both the appeals merit consideration, in the result, the following:
ORDER i) Both the appeals are allowed.
ii) Impugned common judgment is set aside.
NC: 2023:KHC:37641 MFA1003/2017 C/W iii) The matter is remanded back to the Tribunal to the stage of evidence.
iv) Parties can do the needful necessary for adjudication of the claim in accordance with law.
v) Without further notice, parties to appear before the Tribunal on 22.11.2023.

SD/-
